title: Data system deprecation
transcript:
Security Lead: There's a concern about the potential risk of data loss during the immediate deprecation of the outdated patient data system.

On-Call Engineer: I understand the worry, but we need to consider the impact on our patients. A sudden shutdown could cause chaos in the system.

Comms Lead: Perhaps we should explore a hybrid approach? We could migrate some data initially and phase out the rest over time.

Legal Counsel: (nods) That sounds like a viable option. It would mitigate the immediate risk of data loss while allowing for a more manageable transition.

On-Call Engineer: But we'd still be dealing with an outdated system for a while. That could create security vulnerabilities.

Security Lead: Exactly. I'd prefer a full migration to the new system as soon as possible.

Comms Lead: (interrupting) But a full migration could cause prolonged disruption of patient care services. We don't want to put patients at risk like that.

Legal Counsel: (pauses, then) Alright, then we'll go with the hybrid approach. It's not perfect, but it seems to be the least disruptive option available.

On-Call Engineer: I'll take ownership of the hybrid approach, ensuring the migration runs as smoothly as possible.

Security Lead: (sighs) Fine, but I'll need to monitor the patient data closely during the migration. I can't have potential security risks lingering for an extended period.

Legal Counsel: Understood. And we'll maintain backups of the deprecated data for a year, as a precaution.

On a lighter note:

Comms Lead: Hey, have you heard the new coffee in the break room?

On-Call Engineer: Really? I was wondering where that aroma was coming from!

Comms Lead: Yeah, it's amazing! I think it's a new blend. You should try it out!

On-Call Engineer: (smiling) I'll have to remember to grab a cup on my way out. Thanks for the tip!

Title: Decision on Hybrid Approach for Patient Data System Deprecation

Record: The team has decided to implement a hybrid approach for deprecating the outdated patient data system. This strategy aims to mitigate immediate risks of data loss by continuously monitoring patient data during migration. Backups of deprecated data will be maintained for a period of one year. This approach allows for a phased migration, reducing user burden and providing a more manageable transition process. The decision was reached following discussions and does not involve immediate deprecation, full migration to the new system, partial migration with delay, or prolonged exposure to potential security risks.
